cards.text: Jesus is still answering His disciples, who asked when the temple would fall and what the sign would be (Luke 21:7). He's just told them Jerusalem will be surrounded by armies (Luke 21:20). Now He speaks of signs in the sun and moon and stars, and of dismay among the nations down on the earth.

cards.question: Down on the earth, what does Jesus say has the nations bewildered?

cards.text: Then Jesus says men will faint from fear and anxiety over what is coming upon the earth. Friend, I nearly fainted every time that junk drawer rattled open, and it was always just somebody hunting for tape.

cards.question: Jesus says men will faint because the powers of the heavens will be shaken.

cards.text: And now comes the moment all of this has been building to. At that time, Jesus says, they will see someone coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

cards.question: Who does Jesus say they will see coming in a cloud with power and great glory?

cards.text: Everybody's fainting. Hearts pounding. Then Jesus tells His listeners what to do when these things begin to happen, and it is NOT what the rest of the crowd is doing.

cards.question: When these things begin to happen, what does Jesus tell His listeners to do?

answers.text: Stand up and lift up your heads
Kneel down and cover your faces
Lie low and wait it all out

cards.question: Jesus tells them to lift up their heads, because their ___ is drawing near.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them a parable: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees.”

cards.question: In Jesus' parable, when the trees sprout leaves, what can you see for yourself is near?

cards.text: See leaves, know summer. No calendar needed. That's me at my oven: no timer, I just smell that batch turning golden and I KNOW.

cards.question: So also, Jesus says, when you see these things happening, know that the ___ of God is near.

cards.text: Then Jesus says, “Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away until all these things have happened.”

cards.question: Jesus sets heaven and earth beside His own words. Which does He say will never pass away?
Jesus says heaven and earth will pass away.

cards.text: Then Jesus turns it into a warning: “But watch yourselves.” He says their hearts could get weighed down.

cards.question: What does Jesus name among the things that can weigh their hearts down?
If their hearts get weighed down, how does Jesus say that day will come upon them?

cards.text: The worries of life, friend. Bills. Group chats. The inbox at 9 p.m. You're staring so hard at all that, you never see the snare until you're standing in it.

cards.question: Jesus says the day He's warning about will come only on the people of Jerusalem.

cards.text: So Jesus says to keep watch at ALL times, and pray. Friend, that is the exact opposite of the snooze button.

cards.question: Jesus tells them to pray for the ___ to escape all that is about to happen, and to ___ before the Son of Man.

cards.text: That's where Jesus' sermon ends. And every day, Jesus teaches at the temple.

cards.question: Jesus teaches at the temple every day. Where does He go out to spend the night every evening?
Early in the morning, all the people would come to hear Jesus at the temple.

cards.text: All the people, early in the morning. No snooze button for THIS crowd, friend. When that's the Teacher, you set three alarms and get up on the first one.

findings.problem: Stop 3, card 1 quotes "But watch yourselves.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The question asks which thing bewilders the nations, so its wrong answers must be real details from the Bible. 'The silence of the birds' is not a real Bible detail.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

findings.problem: The Son of Man first appears here, and no card says who He is. The baker is never told that this is the name Jesus uses for Himself.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: 'Everybody's fainting. Hearts pounding.' stretches Luke 21:26, which says 'Men will faint.' It does not say everybody, and it says nothing about pounding hearts. 'The rest of the crowd' also gives the fainting men a name the text doesn't use. This is a storyteller line, not one of Papa Dorin's own jokes.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The card retells the fainting from Luke 21:26 but cites only Luke 21:28. The fainting line is also a recap of an earlier card.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The setup says the answer is NOT what the fainting crowd is doing. That rules out the two fear-shaped wrong answers on card 8, 'Kneel down and cover your faces' and 'Lie low and wait it all out.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'Lie low and wait it all out' sounds more casual and modern than the other two answers, so the answers don't sound alike.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats Luke 21:30, which card 2 already asked about, and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: This story card goes back to the worries of life and the snare from Luke 21:34, which cards 2 and 3 already covered. It doesn't move the passage forward. Its joke also blends the modern comparison (bills, group chats, the inbox) with the Bible image of the snare.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The last card only repeats Luke 21:38, which card 10 already asked about, and adds a joke. This is the last passage in its story group, so no 'story isn't over' line is needed, and the card has nothing new to tell.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.
